source: Ubergraph (https://ubergraph.apps.renci.org/sparql), NCBITaxon rdfs:subClassOf closure as served, including inferred edges
what_this_is: The taxonomy the law-scope engine walks. `ancestors` is the clades a taxon is inside, most specific first. Membership is read from the ontology; nothing here is a hand-maintained parent table, which is what it replaces.
what_this_is_not: Not a phylogeny and not a statement about evolutionary distance. NCBI taxonomy is a nomenclatural hierarchy: it says what a clade CONTAINS, which is all a scope check needs, and says nothing about divergence times or relatedness. A law scoped to a clade is calibrated on that clade, and being inside it is necessary for the law to apply, not sufficient for the law to be right.

held_out.rule: held-out taxa are never keys here and are filtered out of every ancestor list; the build fails if one reaches the output. A non-bird has no bird ancestor, so this removes nothing a scope check needs.
